conventions.convention: For finite graph families, “free” means free of induced copies; complements retain the same vertex set.
H+ adds a vertex adjacent exactly to the two distinguished vertices and makes the distinguished pair adjacent; H− instead makes that pair nonadjacent.
A c-restricted set is a c-sparse or c-dense nonempty induced vertex set, with the dense count excluding the vertex itself.
A_TM and HALT_TM contain only valid encoded machine/input pairs using the stated self-delimiting word code; malformed binary words are not members.
Recognizers accept exactly the positive instances and may diverge on negative ones; deciders additionally halt on every input.
An asymptotic O(g(n)) bound holds only from a threshold n₀ onward and supplies no exact bound at all short input lengths.
NP is defined by polynomial-time verification with polynomially bounded binary certificates, and coNP takes complements inside the same binary ambient language.
A polynomial-time many-one reduction preserves membership in the direction x∈A iff f(x)∈B, so P, NP, and coNP membership transfer from target to source.

load_bearing.statement: Under its stated anticonnected-block, mixedness, and complete-or-mutually-η-sparse hypotheses, cliques and sufficiently small indexed induced patterns in the auxiliary graph lift to induced ambient patterns; an adjacent distinguished pattern lifts to H+ under the stricter bound.
Under either stated star-subdivision or special-vertex obstruction hypothesis, the auxiliary graph J has a clique or stable set of size at least |J|^c for some c∈(0,1).
Under its equal-block complete-or-mutually-y^a-sparse hypotheses and a≥5/c+1, a clique or stable set of size at least |I|^c in J yields a y^4-restricted union of whole blocks.
If a finite family satisfies either stated obstruction hypothesis, then that family is wonderful.

A hypothetical decider for A_TM yields a deterministic one-tape machine D_H such that D_H accepts the recoded code of M iff M does not accept that recoded code, for every coded machine M whose input alphabet contains Σ₂.
The language A_TM is not decidable.
The language HALT_TM is recognizable but not decidable.
A verifier for L is a polynomial-time decidable binary relation with a polynomial certificate bound, satisfying x∈L iff it has a bounded accepted certificate.
If A≤pB, then B∈P implies A∈P, B∈NP implies A∈NP, and B∈coNP implies A∈coNP.

concerns.concern: [L1] states without qualifications that an induced copy in J lifts block-by-block and that an H copy lifts to H+. The cited lifting lemma requires (q−1)η<1 and (q−1)η<1/2 respectively, and its stated form uses an indexed copy. Step 2.2 later derives the inequalities in the applications, but [L1] itself is an overstrong cited fact.

Step 1.1 applies [L2] with M=D_H, but [L2] quantifies over coded machines whereas the diagonal lemma only asserts a deterministic one-tape machine D_H. [L3] supplies a code only for a machine already presented as coded. A normalization/coding step is needed before writing ⌜D_H⌝.

Step 1.2 turns the asymptotic assertion that every branch halts within O(n^k) into an exact all-n bound cn^k. The library's O convention applies only for n≥n₀; finite short input lengths need separate handling, or the bound should use c(n+1)^k.

Step 2.1 says that [L3] implies a uniform code-length bound linear in |bin(n)| for the hard-wired machine P_n. [L3] only records that codes are finite transition-table tuples; the asserted compiler-size estimate is not established. A weaker explicit sublinear-in-n estimate would still suffice for the conclusion.

[L1] attributes the implication from 0<|N(v)∩B_i|<|B_i| to “v is mixed on B_i” to the cited mixed-anticonnected lemma. That lemma starts after mixedness is assumed; the preliminary implication instead follows immediately from the complete/anticomplete definition for the singleton pair {v},B_i.
